measures.title: Cuyahoga County – Proposed Tax Levy (Additional): Board of Developmental Disabilities
measures.summary: A new property tax of up to 2.25 mills for ten years for the Cuyahoga County Board of Developmental Disabilities, to operate its programs and services and to acquire, build, renovate, finance, maintain and operate its facilities. The County Fiscal Officer estimates it will collect $99,684,616 a year, which amounts to $79 for each $100,000 of the Fiscal Officer's market value. Collection would start in 2026, first due in 2027.
measures.yesMeans: The new 2.25-mill developmental disabilities levy is collected for ten years.
measures.noMeans: The new levy is not collected.

measures.title: Cuyahoga County – Proposed Tax Levy (Renewal and Increase): Health and Human Services
measures.summary: Renews an existing 4.7-mill county property tax and adds 2.5 mills, for a total of up to 7.2 mills for ten years, to supplement county general fund spending on health and human or social services. The County Fiscal Officer estimates it will collect $261,527,652 a year, which amounts to $196 for each $100,000 of the Fiscal Officer's market value. Collection would start in 2026, first due in 2027.
measures.yesMeans: The 4.7-mill levy is renewed and increased to 7.2 mills for ten years.
measures.noMeans: Neither the renewal nor the increase is approved.

measures.title: Cuyahoga County – Proposed Charter Amendment: Council Confirmation of Board Removals
measures.summary: Amends Article II, Section 2.03 and Article VI, Section 6.04 of the county charter. When the County Executive removes a member of a board, agency, commission or authority created under the charter, a board whose members general law has county commissioners appoint, or a special board created by agreement or court order, County Council would have to confirm the removal.
measures.yesMeans: County Council would have to confirm the County Executive's removal of members of these boards and commissions.
measures.noMeans: The charter is not changed; these removals would not need Council confirmation.

measures.title: Cuyahoga County – Proposed Charter Amendment: Director of Law
measures.summary: Amends Article V, Section 5.06 of the county charter to make the Director of Law the primary legal representative for labor matters, non-litigation employment matters, public records, risk management, and non-litigation contracts and other legal instruments the County Executive enters into, and to give written opinions and legal advice to county officials and entities. It states that county officials may still seek advice from the Prosecuting Attorney, that the Prosecutor's powers are not limited, and that the Director of Law may not handle any litigation for the county unless the Prosecuting Attorney refers it.
measures.yesMeans: The charter would set out the Director of Law's duties and limits as described.
measures.noMeans: The charter section on the Director of Law stays as it is.

measures.title: Cuyahoga County – Proposed Charter Amendment: Charter Review Commission Appointments
measures.summary: Amends Article XII, Section 12.09 of the county charter on who appoints the Charter Review Commission. Four members would be appointed by the County Executive without Council confirmation, four by County Council without the Executive's approval, and one by the County Executive subject to Council confirmation.
measures.yesMeans: Charter Review Commission members would be appointed as described (4 by the Executive, 4 by Council, 1 by the Executive with Council confirmation).
measures.noMeans: The current appointment rules for the Charter Review Commission stay in place.
